asym_test: Interaction chi2(1, N=2352)=2.23, p=.14, OR=1.20 [0.91-1.48] (n.s.; numerically time>space)

S_on_T_stat: Pooled ANOVA over Exps 1-3: subjective size on duration estimates F(1,146)=24.25, p<.001, eta2p=.15; size x illusion type n.s. (ps>=.082); no per-experiment test reported

justification: Authors' only tests pool the 3 between-subject experiments with illusion type as a factor; size effect did not interact with illusion type, and the authors state bidirectional interference for all three illusions. No per-experiment p values, so flag: SYMMETRIC rests on pooled tests.

S_on_T_stat: Pooled ANOVA: subjective size on duration F(1,146)=24.25, p<.001; no size x illusion interaction (ps>=.082)
T_on_S_stat: Pooled: duration on size F(1,146)=128.41, p<.001; Muller-Lyer duration effect 0.22 (illusion-type interaction F(2,146)=18.44, p<.001); per-illusion p not reported

justification: Coded by significant within-group asymmetry test. Text inconsistency: the Results sentence says time-on-space was larger in the young, but the Discussion says the space-on-time asymmetry held in the young, and the authors' posted R script (t.test(time task, space task)) gives t=+2.2, so space-on-time is larger. Authors state both groups showed significant bidirectional interference (no per-group p).
